questions.explanation: Let B = x, so A = x + 5. Then 2x + 5 = 35, giving x = 15 and A = 20.

questions.explanation: Father + son = 4x + x = 5x = 50, so the son's age x = 10.

questions.question: The ages of two persons are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their sum is 56. The younger person's age is
questions.explanation: The sum has 7 parts, so one part = 8. The younger is 3 × 8 = 24.

questions.question: Two brothers differ in age by 4 years. If the elder is 19 years old, the younger one's age 4 years ago was
questions.explanation: Younger now = 19 − 4 = 15. Four years ago he was 15 − 4 = 11.

questions.question: Five years ago a father was 4 times as old as his son. The sum of their present ages is 50. The father's present age is
questions.explanation: Let the son be s and the father f. f − 5 = 4(s − 5) and f + s = 50. Then f = 4s − 15, so 5s − 15 = 50, giving s = 13 and f = 37.

questions.question: The ages of two persons are in the ratio 4 : 5. After 5 years the ratio will be 5 : 6. The age of the elder person now is
questions.explanation: Ages are 4x and 5x. (4x + 5)/(5x + 5) = 5/6 gives 24x + 30 = 25x + 25, so x = 5. The elder is 25.

questions.question: A is 9 years older than B. In 10 years A will be twice as old as B was 10 years ago. A's present age is
questions.explanation: Let B = b, so A = b + 9. A + 10 = 2(b − 10) gives b + 19 = 2b − 20, so b = 39 and A = 48.

questions.question: The average age of a family of 5 members is 24 years and the youngest member is 8 years old. The average age of the family (the other 4 members) at the time of the youngest's birth was
questions.explanation: Total age now = 120, so the other four total 112. Eight years ago each was 8 years younger: 112 − 4 × 8 = 80. Average = 80 ÷ 4 = 20 years.

questions.question: A mother is 3 times as old as her daughter. After 12 years she will be twice as old as her daughter. The daughter's present age is
questions.explanation: Let the daughter be d. 3d + 12 = 2(d + 12) gives d = 12 and the mother is 36.

questions.question: A father is 7 times as old as his son. After 4 years he will be 4 times as old. The father's present age is
questions.explanation: Let the son be s. 7s + 4 = 4(s + 4) gives 3s = 12, so s = 4 and the father is 28.

questions.question: The ages of two persons are in the ratio 5 : 7 and the difference of their ages is 8 years. The elder's age is
questions.explanation: The difference is 2 parts = 8, so one part = 4. The elder is 7 × 4 = 28.

The present ages of Sameer and Anita are in the ratio 5 : 4. Three years from now the ratio will be 11 : 9. Anita's age 3 years ago was
questions.explanation: Ages are 5x and 4x. (5x + 3)/(4x + 3) = 11/9 gives 45x + 27 = 44x + 33, so x = 6. Anita is 24 now and was 21 three years ago.

questions.question: A father is 30 years older than his son, who is now 10 years old. In how many years will the father be 3 times as old as the son?
questions.explanation: Father is 40. After n years: 40 + n = 3(10 + n), so 40 + n = 30 + 3n, giving n = 5.

questions.question: The ages of A, B and C are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 and their sum is 100. B's age 10 years ago was
questions.explanation: Total parts = 10, so one part = 10. B = 30 now and 20 ten years ago.

questions.question: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. Ten years ago A was half as old as B. The sum of their present ages is
questions.explanation: Ages are 3k and 4k. 3k − 10 = (4k − 10)/2 gives 6k − 20 = 4k − 10, so k = 5. Ages are 15 and 20, sum 35.

questions.question: A man is 24 years older than his son. In two years his age will be twice the age of his son. The man's present age is
questions.explanation: Let the son be s, the man s + 24. s + 26 = 2(s + 2) gives s = 22 and the man is 46.

questions.explanation: F − 3 = 7(S − 3) gives F = 7S − 18. F + 3 = 4(S + 3) gives F = 4S + 9. Equating: 3S = 27, so S = 9 and F = 45.
